root_cause: The fast-path whitelist regex in rich/cells.py, "^[\u0020-\u006f\u00a0\u02ff\u0370-\u0482]*$", had two typos. \u006f ('o') should have been \u007e ('~'), so p-z, {, |, } and ~ fell off the fast path. The hyphen between \u00a0 and \u02ff was missing, so only those two code points matched instead of the Latin-1/Latin Extended range. It also left out box-drawing characters (U+2500 block), which rich emits constantly for tables and panels. Everything outside the class went through the slow per-character width lookup.
best_solution: Rewrite the character class as ^[\u0020-\u007e\u00a0-\u02ff\u0370-\u0482\u2500-\u25FF]*$: all printable ASCII, the Latin-1 and Latin Extended range with the hyphen restored, Greek/Cyrillic as before, and box drawing, block elements and geometric shapes. The reasoning from the statement: reading the regex shows \u006f is 'o', an obvious off-by-one for \u007e, and '\u00a0\u02ff' is a range missing its '-'. The box-drawing addition follows from what rich itself renders: every table and panel border is U+2500-U+257F, and those are 1 cell wide in rich's own CELL_WIDTHS. Separately, segment.py's Segment.split_cells gains an 'assert cut >= 0' and an Args docstring. No test checks that part.
acceptable_alternatives: Any class that matches every printable ASCII char (0x20-0x7e) and the U+2500 box-drawing chars, and rejects emoji and CJK, passes. A narrower box range such as \u2500-\u257F is arguably more correct: rich's own table gives U+25FD and U+25FE a width of 2, so gold's \u25FF upper bound misclassifies those two, though no test checks them. Adding \u007f passes the tests but is semantically dubious. The segment.py assert is optional.
hidden_test_demands: tests/test_cells.py::test_is_single_cell_widths imports the private name _is_single_cell_widths from rich.cells (it must stay a module-level match callable). It asserts a truthy result for every string.printable char with ord >= 32, and for every char of BOX = "┌─┬┐│ ││├─┼┤│ ││├─┼┤├─┼┤│ ││└─┴┘" (U+2500 block). It asserts a falsy result for the emoji 💩 and 😽 and for the hiragana わ, さ, び. The BOX assertion (line 75) is the part the statement never mentions.
locating_signals: "regex used to select the fast path for strings with single-width characters" points straight at rich/cells.py _is_single_cell_widths, whose comment says 'Regex to match sequence of the most common character ranges'. Grepping for 'fast path' finds the '# Fast path with all 1 cell characters' comment in segment.py split_cells. The regex is not named in the statement but is found in a few greps. The needed ranges are not stated at all.
our_outcome_summary: 0/4 passed (v4, v6, v7, v8 all false). v4, v6 and v7 found the right line within about 15 steps. Then they looped on edit_file, getting 'old_string not found' 70, 38 and 44 times, until the 6-minute session timeout, and produced empty patches. The model sent old_string with a doubled backslash ('\\u0020') while the source holds a single-backslash escape '\u0020' inside a non-raw string, and it never changed strategy. v8 hit 9 of the same failures, then fell back to write_file/run_command. It submitted a patch changing only \u006f to \u007f: no hyphen fix for \u00a0-\u02ff and no box-drawing range. It failed at tests/test_cells.py:75 (BOX char, AssertionError: assert None). None of the candidate regexes in any config included U+2500-U+25FF (v4: 007e/00a0-02ff/0370-04ff; v7 went up to 058F), so even a working editor would not have passed.
generalizable_lesson: (1) Harness: when the target line contains literal backslash escapes (\uXXXX, \d, \n inside a str or regex literal), JSON-encoded old_string gets double-escaped. After two identical 'old_string not found' failures, the agent should switch to line-number replacement, or to a python -c script that reads the file and does str.replace on the exact bytes it printed with repr(). The edit tool should also retry with backslash-normalized matching and name the nearest matching line. (2) Semantics: when fixing a fast-path whitelist or cache or shortcut, derive it from the slow-path oracle instead of guessing. Enumerate candidate characters, assert that fast_path(c) implies slow_path(c) == 1, and include characters the codebase itself emits (grep the repo for non-ASCII literals such as box-drawing borders). Hidden tests often pin exactly those.
